findings.evidence: RealForm.lean:61-70: the inputs are `(hinj : ∀ x, Injective (i x))` and `hmax : ∀ x`, but the body only uses `FiberBundle.t2Space F W x`, `FiberBundle.t2Space G V x`, `VectorBundle.finiteDimensional ℝ F W x` and `isBaseChange_complex_of_isMaximalTotallyReal (hinj x) (hmax x)`.
findings.fix: Add a module-level `ContinuousLinearMap.complexificationEquivOfIsMaximalTotallyReal (f : W →L[ℝ] V) (hf : Injective f) (hmax : IsMaximalTotallyReal _ (LinearMap.range f)) [FiniteDimensional ℝ W] [T2Space W] [T2Space V] ... : (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] W) ≃L[ℂ] V`, next to `liftBaseChangeComplex` in `Topology/Algebra/Module/Complexification`. Prove its tmul/apply lemmas there, then define the bundle diffeomorphism fibrewise as `fun x ↦ (i x).complexificationEquivOfIsMaximalTotallyReal (hinj x) (hmax x)`.
findings.issue: `maximalRealFormComplexificationEquiv` builds the equivalence at a single point `x`, yet it requires `hinj : ∀ x, Injective (i x)`, `hmax : ∀ x, ...` and the `FiberBundle`/`VectorBundle` instances. It only uses `hinj x`, `hmax x`, and two facts taken from the bundle: each fibre is Hausdorff and finite-dimensional. Someone with the hypotheses at just one fibre, or a plain module pair that is not part of a bundle, cannot use it. Its `_tmul`, `_toLinearEquiv` and `_apply` lemmas inherit the same over-strong signature.

summary: The fibre-level complexification equivalence is a single-module fact, but it is stated only inside the bundle setting and demands injectivity and maximality at every point to build one fibre. Everything else sits at the natural level.
